title: Global Logistics Fleet Tracking Scaling
business: Logistics companies managing millions of real-time IoT sensor updates from a global fleet.
problem: A single-node PostgreSQL instance hits write-throughput bottlenecks and storage limits when processing high-velocity telemetry data from thousands of vehicles simultaneously.
solution: Azure Cosmos DB for PostgreSQL distributes PostgreSQL tables across multiple nodes, allowing the database to scale horizontally by partitioning data based on a distribution column, such as a vehicle identifier.
steps: Provision an Azure Cosmos DB for PostgreSQL cluster.
Select a distribution column, such as vehicle_id, to serve as the shard key.
Execute the distribution function to partition existing tables across the worker nodes.
Configure application connection strings to route queries through the coordinator node.
outcome: The system achieves horizontal write scalability, allowing the database to handle increasing telemetry ingestion rates by adding more worker nodes to the cluster.
limitation: Queries that do not include the distribution column in the WHERE clause may result in cross-shard communication, which increases latency; verify this by checking the query plan for distributed execution overhead.
